quotes.text: Most architects assume that because their logic app is in Azure, their data stays in Azure. But with managed connectors, that's not true.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights an often overlooked networking and security flaw of managed connectors.

quotes.text: High-functioning agents require sub-200 millisecond round trips for natural turn-taking. And if the plumbing takes longer than the thinking, the entire orchestration falls apart.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Connects integration latency directly to AI agent performance.

takeaways: Managed connectors add hidden latency, throttling limits and retry storms because data passes through a shared middleware layer you do not control.
gRPC with Protocol Buffers and persistent streams such as WebSockets reduce payload size, CPU overhead and empty polling traffic compared with REST and JSON.
Queue-front high-speed flows with a durable buffer like Azure Service Bus and move to Logic Apps Standard with built-in connectors to keep data inside your virtual network.
hook: Managed connectors feel like the easy button, but under load they become a brittle bottleneck of throttling, latency and retry storms. This episode shows integration architects why the fix is a protocol-level shift to gRPC, persistent streams, queue-fronted resilience and built-in Logic Apps connectors.
